clue.text: Offensive plot invalid here

definitions.note: a place where someone ill lies, so the definition names a location

parts.note: a sick joke is an offensive one
a bed is a garden plot for flowers

explanation.surface: An offensive scheme is declared null and void at this point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invalid' reads as 'void', but here it is the noun, a sick person, and 'here' makes the definition the place where such a person lies.
explanation.definitionFit: A patient who is unwell is confined to this, so it is where an invalid stays.

clue.text: Bad man said to reform good one?

indicators.note: to reform something is to reshape it, so these letters are put into a new order

parts.note: a good person is a saint, abbreviated St

explanation.surface: A villain is reported to have turned into a decent person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to reform' rearranges SAID into SADI; 'good one?' is a saint, ST, the question mark owning up to the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who takes pleasure in cruelty is a classic example of a wicked man.

clue.text: See 20
One's work's stuck up, as William in the reign of Charles III?

parts.note: Bill is the short form of the name William

parts.words: in the reign of Charles III
parts.note: the reign of Charles III comes after that of Elizabeth, ER, so it is POST-ER, after ER

explanation.surface: Someone whose handiwork is pasted up high, like a future William serving under King Charles.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is the crossword abbreviation for Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth; the reign of the next monarch is 'post ER'. The puzzle predates Charles's accession, so the clue looked ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who pastes up advertising placards has a job whose output is stuck on walls.

clue.text: Fish left in books to fill handed-out bread?

indicators.note: one piece goes into the other so it fills its middle

parts.note: the dole is state benefit money handed out, and bread is slang for money
the verso is the left-hand page of an open book

explanation.surface: A fish is left among the books to pad out a charity bread hand-out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to fill' signals the container. 'bread' is slang for money, so the British state unemployment benefit is handed-out bread; the verso is the left-hand page of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a prized flatfish of European waters, named after the Kent port.

clue.text: Rob, then save a bit of old brass

parts.note: to sack a town is to plunder or rob it
save in the sense 'except' means but

explanation.surface: Thieve, then keep back a piece of antique brassware.
explanation.walkthrough: 'save' looks like a verb but is the preposition meaning 'except', i.e. but; 'brass' is the orchestral section, not the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: This early trombone is an antique brass instrument, one item of the old brass section.

clue.text: Good to be in peaceful surroundings, given uprising, it is plain

indicators.note: the good letter sits inside the word for peaceful

parts.note: serene means peaceful, and here it surrounds another letter

indicators.note: in a down clue an uprising reads the word from bottom to top, so it is turned round

parts.note: taken as written before being turned

explanation.surface: Being good amid calm, given a revolt, is simple enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the container and 'given uprising' the reversal, apt in a down light; 'is' joins to the definition 'plain', which is the noun for grassland, not 'simple'.
explanation.definitionFit: This vast stretch of Tanzanian grassland is a famous African plain.

clue.text: Company gloated

definitions.meaning: a group of people working together, such as a ship's or film company
an old past tense of crow, to boast or gloat

explanation.definitionFit: A team of workers is a company, and the archaic past of crow means gloated.

clue.text: Catch up, then strike hard in proportional representation

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to catch hold of is to grab
to rap is to strike sharply
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Seize something, then hit it hard in an electoral system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns GRAB into BARG. 'proportional representation' poses as the voting system but is a picture showing quantities as bars of proportional length.
explanation.definitionFit: This chart represents quantities with bars whose lengths are proportional to the values.

clue.text: Tie lease up over time, or move in an instant?

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece over another sits above it, so it comes first
in a down clue up reads both words from bottom to top together

parts.note: to rope something is to tie it
to let a property is to lease it

explanation.surface: Tie up a lease over time, or vanish and reappear at once?
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses both synonyms together to give TELEPOR, and 'over' sets that above the T in the down light. The question mark flags the sci-fi definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In science fiction this means transport instantly from one place to another without crossing the space between.

clue.text: Live comfortably by end of road

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: to live well is to live comfortably

explanation.surface: Live in comfort beside where the road runs out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Live' is the verb, to reside, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside somewhere is to live there.

clue.text: Sort of column a little irregular: bet reviews taken the wrong way

indicators.note: the run of letters is read backwards, from right to left
a little of the words is a short run of their letters

explanation.surface: Some pillar is slightly uneven: wagered verdicts are misunderstood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a little' picks the run LARBETREV from 'irregular: bet reviews', and 'taken the wrong way' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: The spine is the vertebral column, so this adjective describes a kind of column.

clue.text: Relative set out plain, though not originally

indicators.note: set out suggests the letters are laid out afresh in another order

parts.note: taken as written before being rearranged

indicators.note: without its original, first letter

parts.note: plain in the sense obvious means apparent

explanation.surface: A family member is laid bare, though not at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges SET into STE; 'not originally' drops the first letter of APPARENT to leave PPARENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A parent by marriage rather than blood counts as a relative.

clue.text: See 19
In the red, a rent adjustment needed as running account

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go inside the word for a red

parts.note: a red is a communist, informally a commie or commy

indicators.note: an adjustment changes the letters' order

parts.note: taken as written before being rearranged

explanation.surface: Overdrawn, a tenancy charge needs fixing as an ongoing tally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the red' looks like 'overdrawn' but splits: 'In' is the container signal and 'the red' a communist. 'adjustment' rearranges the rent letters to ENTAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A running commentary is a continuous account of events as they happen.

clue.text: Smiling bouncer discovers buyer stashing speed

indicators.note: the buyer hides the speed word away inside

parts.note: a shopper is someone who buys
pace means speed

explanation.surface: A grinning nightclub doorman catches a customer hiding amphetamines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stashing' signals the container. A space hopper is a large inflatable ball with handles, often printed with a grinning face, that children sit on and bounce.
explanation.definitionFit: This bouncing toy ball traditionally bears a big grinning face, so it is a smiling bouncer.

clue.text: Love a fair helping of bother?

parts.note: ado is fuss or bother
a ration is a fair share or helping

explanation.surface: Is affection simply a decent portion of trouble?
explanation.walkthrough: 'a fair helping of bother' reads as a quantity of trouble; the helping follows the bother in the answer, with 'of' as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoration is deep love and worship.

clue.text: Old writers bound to find system of working not closed

parts.note: pens are writing instruments
to bound is to leap or hop

explanation.surface: Ancient authors are sure to discover a way of working that is open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound' looks like 'certain' but is the verb to leap. An OPEN SHOP is a workplace where union membership is not required, the opposite of a closed shop.
explanation.definitionFit: This workplace arrangement admits non-union workers, unlike a closed shop.

clue.text: Universally accepted answer, a funny way to be caught

parts.note: U is the British film certificate for universal, suitable for all

indicators.note: funny suggests something odd, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written before being rearranged
taken as written before being rearranged

explanation.surface: An answer everyone agrees on is a comic way to be found out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'funny' rearranges ANSWER A into NAWARES. 'way to be caught' is fair since one is caught unawares, by surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Being taken by surprise is being caught off guard, so this adverb describes the manner of capture.

clue.text: Uproar from black and white endangered instrument, might you say?

indicators.note: the phrase signals a word spoken that sounds like another

parts.note: a panda is a black and white endangered animal and a harmonium a keyboard instrument, said together quickly

explanation.surface: Chaos breaks out over a rare monochrome musical instrument, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: PANDA HARMONIUM said quickly runs together into the word for chaos; the homophone is loose, and 'might you say?' admits it.
explanation.definitionFit: This word means wild noise and chaos, a synonym of uproar.

clue.text: Regularly written blurb wasted on Eminem's music — do pop fans love it?

indicators.note: every other letter of the word is written down, starting with the first

parts.note: to blow money is to waste it, past tense blew
Eminem is a rapper, so his music is rap

explanation.surface: Every other line of promotional copy is squandered on hip-hop; do pop lovers adore it?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly written' takes alternate letters of BLURB, giving BUB. The definition is a playful one: people who like popping things love this packing material.
explanation.definitionFit: This packing material of air cells is notoriously satisfying to pop, so poppers love it.

clue.text: Plain wrong choice for Henry after eleven cans of special brew?

indicators.note: a brew mixes ingredients up, so these letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A dowdy mistake by Henry, after downing eleven tins of strong lager?
explanation.walkthrough: Special Brew is a strong British lager, and the joke says Henry chose his wife drunk. Henry VIII found Anne of Cleves plain and soon divorced her.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry VIII's fourth wife, whom he thought unattractive, was his mistaken choice of bride.

clue.text: Information from all corners of the globe?

definitions.meaning: reports of recent events, i.e. information
the four compass points, north, east, west and south, abbreviated

explanation.definitionFit: Reports of recent happenings are information, and the four compass point letters span the globe.

clue.text: Monstrous joke about king, one from Italian city, guillotined

indicators.note: the joke word goes around the king letter

parts.note: a gag is a joke
R is the abbreviation for rex, king

indicators.note: the guillotine cuts off the head, so the first letter goes

parts.note: a Mantuan is a native of Mantua in northern Italy

explanation.surface: An awful quip about a monarch and a citizen of an Italian town who lost his head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the container; 'guillotined' takes off the head, the first letter, of the citizen of Mantua.
explanation.definitionFit: Something enormous and gigantic, like Rabelais's giant, may be called monstrous in size.

clue.text: One soldier and another 22

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier
a second soldier, a soldier ant

explanation.surface: One trooper and a second one make a monster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' means another soldier: soldier ants are a caste of ant. '22' is the answer to 22 across, used as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something enormous, like a huge creature, matches the meaning of the cross-referenced word for monstrous.

clue.text: See 4
Instrument causing damage when attached to one short whip

parts.note: harm is damage
on can mean attached to, as a lid is on
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: short means missing its final letter

parts.note: a cat, short for cat-o'-nine-tails, is a whip

explanation.surface: An instrument that causes harm when fixed to a short whip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts the last letter from CAT, leaving CA.
explanation.definitionFit: This small reed instrument is played by blowing, a mouth organ.

clue.text: Walk, though don't start to walk

indicators.note: telling the walking word not to start means it loses its opening letter

parts.note: to ramble is to walk for pleasure

explanation.surface: Stroll, but don't begin to stroll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'don't start' removes the R from RAMBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A leisurely stroll is a walk.

clue.text: Father authoritarian, bit of a nag

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
stern means strict or authoritarian

explanation.surface: A strict dad is a bit of a nag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nag' suggests a carping person; here it is a horse, and the PASTERN is part of a horse's leg.
explanation.definitionFit: This part of a horse's foot between fetlock and hoof is a bit of a horse.

clue.text: Unknown quantity cuts meat back after temperature for you personally once

indicators.note: the rest follows the temperature letter
the unknown letter cuts into the meat word
the meat word is read backwards

parts.note: flesh is meat
in algebra x, y and z are unknown quantities

explanation.surface: An unknown slices into meat after warming, for your own sake in the old style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns FLESH into HSELF, 'cuts' puts Y inside it after the H, and 'after' sets all this after T.
explanation.definitionFit: This archaic reflexive pronoun means yourself, used in old English for the second person.
